昨天一个朋友突然在群里吐槽，说某东太狗了，竟然用大数据杀熟，同一个店铺的同一款同一型号商品，她和她父亲分别下单，竟然是不同的价格。


![image.png](https://images.hive.blog/DQme9vJNoNup5h8sQVNBqfHUM9thFj2bZzL6Q3jGDCpv2QF/image.png)
(插图由ChatGPT辅助生成)

我看了一下这个商品，是绿聚能的单反相机替换电池，型号是LP-E6NH，标称电量是2320mAh。

朋友和下单时的价格是140.94元
![c6156f76c5e37c711860f1554da6b61a.png](https://images.hive.blog/DQmf6RGt9quaiWFhHcmcyj8B8X2nmdi4imgSW8Gz6ne42J7/c6156f76c5e37c711860f1554da6b61a.png)

她父亲下单的价格是129.42元。
![dc523b9667e745418b2b5521891aa6b2.png](https://images.hive.blog/DQmba8FSTyx4zLLs575F8ND5W5GTXYY6YFwivrx9nXzUAYQ/dc523b9667e745418b2b5521891aa6b2.png)

朋友作为某东的PLUS会员，买同一款商品，竟然比不是会员的父亲价格还贵，她觉得难以理解且难以忍受，所以来群里吐槽！

我看了她发的订单中的电池信息后，手欠地去搜索了这款电池，嗯，找到的是同一店铺的同一款商品的同一个型号。

但是你猜某东给我的价格是多少？

当当当当，答案揭晓，竟然是109.62元！比朋友和她父亲买到的价格都低！
![876fbc0bd2b284ada0e26659fbbe868a.png](https://images.hive.blog/DQmXbFsNzMz2yRwNx65EW7e75vZb5s1Rb15gXLmuyTgTEq9/876fbc0bd2b284ada0e26659fbbe868a.png)

要知道，这电池也不过就是一百多元，现在朋友的价格和我的价格竟然相差31元，近30%的差价，这也太恐怖😱啦！

我把这价格发到群里，狠狠地扎了朋友的心，朋友看完我的价格，心都碎了。💔

但你以为这就算完了？群友们看我扎了朋友的心，纷纷上来晒价格，结果不但又狠狠地扎了朋友的心，我的心也被深深地刺痛了。

群友一的价格
![72169009d5d9249e7891ce786e9bb20b.png](https://images.hive.blog/DQmV9K7CtzahF8v7y6XookDKJiCebYf3V3ZDBtmrn4yuHrm/72169009d5d9249e7891ce786e9bb20b.png)

群友二的价格
![d1747da3725ace6ab9b18c1add626cee.png](https://images.hive.blog/DQmeGFPurcaeiGpyHtwY6akbEhrxdxbaHHVVUc73NoU9GkG/d1747da3725ace6ab9b18c1add626cee.png)

群友三的价格
![c7fa55b3101901399c889c09fe2d804d.png](https://images.hive.blog/DQmazFJdRJp1uZ2kKVurEBx74izwFUKzaC9CJZpxCjjtRKB/c7fa55b3101901399c889c09fe2d804d.png)

群友四的价格
![12b123d8ea1848049ae39562970b113c.png](https://images.hive.blog/DQmXcfCct3LboQb1i4Wgd5qxSZtjZC8S1VUjCa9CX2RXp3o/12b123d8ea1848049ae39562970b113c.png)

还有更多的价格就不晒了。

怎么评论呢，简直就是一人一价，人人不同，其中不少群友的价格竟然比我的价格还低，呜呜呜，原本想扎朋友的心，结果我也被扎心了。

朋友抓狂，说要怒卸载狗东，并发誓再也不用了。

可是另外一个朋友说了实话，现在何止是某东啊，某宝，某夕，某音，啥啥都是在利用大数据优势给用户画像，然后把用户像猪一样宰！

哎，作为砧板上的鱼肉，我们除了任人宰割，还能做啥呢？毕竟有很多东西在网上买，还是要便利不少。而且线下店铺就不宰人了嘛？只能宰得更狠！


![image.png](https://images.hive.blog/DQmcrHNGP3AtYer2hVmtn7tFZ991zdyLRxDNP62Jui1A2aS/image.png)
(插图由ChatGPT辅助生成)

突然很怀念那个明码实价的时代，也许东西卖得贵，但至少一视同仁的宰啊。总比卖给别人便宜，卖给我贵，让我一个人做冤大头的好呀。

真心希望ZF啥时候好好整治一下大数据杀熟、一人一价的乱象，还消费者朗朗乾坤啊！

现在这情形，让人真的毫无购物的欲望，这经济还如何发展呢？

<center>![PXL_20261016_170255252.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/bozz/242Y3vs2c59Uc26UETcqNDvadapQ1UaMmqK7QEQ9k6CpYxMby1jaffacb2bg3EJw47zbD.jpg)</center>

-----------------------------

After we had finished doing a little bit of shopping at some of the stores alongside the university in Austin, we decided it might be kind of fun to walk around the campus.  Since it was Friday, there was still a lot of people to navigate through.  Students rushing this way and that to classes or whatever other engagements they had.  The campus is quite beautiful at the University of Texas, and they do a really good job of keeping it all in a compact area.  Except for the tennis courts, baseball and softball fields, but I will get to that in a bit.


<center>![PXL_20261016_163018951.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/bozz/23ynUjLTz3avhdcmdRWm2FhKVHdx6jjWySw9MkmU2KxBgq7Ay9NT5nSuoryyJUgYz3Tzg.jpg)</center>


<center>![PXL_20261016_163025109.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/bozz/23zkkemkZVJYh5mKAZc4rEYJc1uctSH3dNQREpbF9SopnrJDrNUxQA6PRUtJhc4KxXgKt.jpg)</center>

------------------------

If you have never heard it before, the motto of Austin is "stay weird", and it is definitely a quirky town full of art and all other kinds of interesting stuff.  There are murals just about everywhere you look, and I tried to get a shot of a few of them as you can see above.


<center>![PXL_20261016_164656532.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/bozz/244UrEyJrxCaC4CjHfxVdc4T8woKUUn4ADga8H7Kex2BiFoyvo6GYsQrHtdMe6ZtH4YrQ.jpg)</center>


<center>![PXL_20261016_164658744.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/bozz/23wgPvQ4k7QPaAzJC5WmpiWXePH2dvjk1WETeZM5eMXaQt81Ff7G1LM7Chg5kLass98be.jpg)</center>

----------------------------

One of the things I really liked about the campus was the Spanish inspired architecture.  The buildings all had this flare to them that kind of reminded you of a city like San Antonio or something like that.  To be fair, San Antonio is only an hour and a half south of Austin.  We will definitely be driving down there for a day if we ever visit Austin again.

We decided to duck into the Student Union to check it out.


<center>![PXL_20261016_164735141.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/bozz/23uFPkg31JnsDgFKUepNUAR1YsTWXbwGeGffJBzfKcdg5RK9B8F4LuzvPmRPoWxKShu7y.jpg)</center>


<center>![PXL_20261016_164741772.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/bozz/23uQjyDnEqJK6xzNoPHo9rBPRUPnWc6mVZZ15NWo2WBTGzuAePd5zEAjSuWa4jmdDrR58.jpg)</center>

-----------------------------

It's a pretty lavish building on the inside, rich with dark woods and what feels like a lot of history though the building itself doesn't look that old. Unfortunately, there was an event going on in the union and they had a lot of the other areas locked or they were requiring a student ID to access them, so we didn't make it much further than the foyer.  It was still pretty cool to check it out.  


<center>![PXL_20261016_165308435.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/bozz/2458QHsCtqnv9mzMYDAFgJBxz2g9F8UmEV35ES84GXz4ofPMdkJppqC9xfAzSDbawaZgu.jpg)</center>

---------------------------

We also found a random statue of George Washington on the campus.  There are actually quite a few statues on campus that we didn't get photos of, but the one of Washington just felt really out of place down in Texas.  My brother in law commented that over at UVA (Virginia) they have a larger statue similar to this one.  Now that makes sense to me being over on the east coast like that.  I would question whether Washington ever actually stepped foot in Texas.  I am guessing no.


<center>![PXL_20261016_165404169.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/bozz/23zGip5yBPMV5YZDoU3LmVjnWXriqSgTu35TtFhtvKybmXCxHqKV6GgF9ty8PAq5E8gux.jpg)</center>


<center>![PXL_20261016_165436313.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/bozz/245ccRnWzv5XpXRJgwZ3pgr4FLp3Kir49o8sEvrB6cwzzAmpLcRbJnUpBWksoevBDeoUT.jpg)</center>

------------------------------------

The focal point of the campus is the large clock tower, but unfortunately, it was being rennovated, so as you can see there is just a bunch of scaffolding all around it.  Back in 1966 on August 1st, there was a mass shooting that took place on this campus.  A 25 year old marine veteran killed 15 people while firing at random from both inside the main tower building and from the observation deck of the tower.  He also injured 31 others before two Austin police officers killed him 96 minutes later.

There are a ton of documentaries about the shooting if you want to dig a little more into it.  


<center>![PXL_20261016_170015661.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/bozz/244xymvt6GqJHWMhvxj9BCD95DYK4Q6eaQ8LTmBKdthFf1jahTC5c14QdZvpgYp5KMFQv.jpg)</center>

-----------------------

Like I said, a lot of the buildings had a really "new" feel to them even though they might actually be quite old.  Either that or the just renovated the exterior of the buildings to make them look fresh.  I don't really know.


<center>![PXL_20261016_170118362.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/bozz/23wgMmZmArusBkwMkQK1nFB886pkLpap3XrGqrZ1fwDX6gg1hGrLv6TWNbQ4gCzNCASWj.jpg)</center>


<center>![PXL_20261016_170120871.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/bozz/23w2jHPipZc45gQGpTE4SWyctm9QPebye5UnesRF5SKQa36btoU4BEtpTQysiin34gmjx.jpg)</center>


<center>![PXL_20261016_170127444.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/bozz/23vsQDCXr8r7wkKj1ZpHDJ7zGFHcAfiUQyv8ZCWz3GfZm9ETvg1UxpvfaBnjK94EJkJs7.jpg)</center>

----------------------------------

As you might imagine, there are cacti everywhere in Texas, and I tried to get some shots of them.  There were certain spots where you really have to pay attention to where you are walking, otherwise you could easily brush up against one of them and really ruin your day!


<center>![PXL_20261016_170228356.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/bozz/23wMWRvXmUhpr6SknVp52sdAaWXEZcqcQbMtgKYRugAsLSyGxAh8te2kHRjwAWyeWa9WR.jpg)</center>


<center>![PXL_20261016_170244712.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/bozz/23w2eXh5RqVHFkc473JWn9geE7LZBf8nWGjZkDuf6gz4JEqz4eh6ciFQVLYQ2k8EMuiCs.jpg)</center>

---------------------------------

Along with cacti, we also saw a ton of the Tesla CyberCabs/RoboTaxi's or CyberTaxis/RoboCabs's, I always get them mixed up.  The automated vehicles were zipping along everywhere taking people from one place to another.  It was pretty impressive to watch them manuevor.  


<center>![PXL_20261016_172016593.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/bozz/243WRkXMLdh1pTA7HJqUy5dugWX5Mqn7FywfXSm9inpZUTGJBktXisrBjDGDfcoy21oCm.jpg)</center>


<center>![PXL_20261016_172029386.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/bozz/243fkPjZ23XvLH8jemc8CnEeW7Fu4aw9eJxrKk6gNkAQqSnxEjsZxob74jQuJqW7UTfFY.jpg)</center>


<center>![PXL_20261016_172903836.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/bozz/245TC7yBoD1f8BEZCYP45MJgAibGWjQCfvCUm7amfLRJGx3PELmNJWKcqDPtvyWTnULqX.jpg)</center>

---------------------------

After leaving campus, we made a quick drive by the capitol building before crossing the expressway to checkout the baseball and softball fields.  As nice as the softball field was, you could tell that baseball is a much bigger deal down in these parts.  The baseball stadium was pretty impressive.


<center>![PXL_20261016_173118348.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/bozz/2432Fbt7ALQM6SGY77AwAJF8quHEXLaYRjboTVmSiMX19QnHrds2VMCfC8xWKxMcBznTS.jpg)</center>


<center>![PXL_20261016_173128691.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/bozz/23rB7nupQNUhNzR6soTZGfXXj8B1R9WQmAqSQCSekWp99p2t4QaKj51k5NAPkGMXQbqMW.jpg)</center>


<center>![PXL_20261016_173140576.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/bozz/241F2QxfY16DPn7USXiQhzSFcjL3JNGg14dYkNXB1utWcjnSvbkXrnqnJ98qTsVzus3hm.jpg)</center>


<center>![PXL_20261016_173154804.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/bozz/243WPiyaHDcaGQZ5ELMSVZ2pxbrwtfR8zFKsaEPHmE3ToAKhtAsxxrj1nnmLqhzSTYZGc.jpg)</center>


<center>![PXL_20261016_173159842.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/bozz/241QRVn6Rkyh73kgGP3Js9FS8jCfs2oXUKXHSAvzxPrrAMawv5m5mWHZnYRCUACDSNdRa.jpg)</center>

-----------------------------------

We got lucky at the softball diamond as the maintenance crews were doing some work, so although the front gates were locked, we simply strolled into the back entrance we saw open and found ourselves walking right onto the field.  There was a guy off in the distance doing some work, but he didn't seem to care that we were there.  

The field is interesting in that the outfield is grass, and the infield is dirt, but all the area everywhere else is turf.  It was still pretty cool to get in and see it. 

<center>![PXL_20261016_180856700.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/bozz/EpJYd8iWLydL5RE214cntUwgY4dhmoQ3so6nvrEdTDoyEB7aPUfufH9R5WaXRKdeAuG.jpg)</center>

---------------------------------

Finally, here's a closer view of a CyberCab.  We also saw a ton of Waymo cars rolling around.  Austin is pretty lousy with self driving vehicles. It's interesting how obtrusive all the sensors are on the Waymo cars versus the Tesla ones.

[source](https://static.independent.co.uk/s3fs-public/thumbnails/image/2017/09/21/12/manchester-united-old-trafford-general-view-2.jpg) I was listening to Paul Merson this week with regard to his comments about Manchester United and he gets it. The club has been living in the past thinking they are a top 4 club in the Premier League and missing out on Champions League football each year is seen as a failure. The harsh truth is the club is a mid table club at best and anything else achieved must be considered over performing. It does not matter if the club has the best manager in the world or the best facilities as whoever is in charge will fail due to the expectations being unrealistic.
[source](https://www.skysports.com/football/story-telling/12860167/man-utds-decade-in-the-dark-lb1-45bn-spent-five-managers-and-no-title) Manchester United las one the Premier League title back in 2012/2013 which is 14 seasons ago and looks further away than ever. Over this period the club has churned through 7 managers and 3 or 4 more caretaker managers or interim managers being the correct terminology. The club have not been shy with the spending either having flashed the cash to the tune of £1.43 billion which is an average of £100 million per season. The problem with having no stability at the top players are bought under one manager for his plan and then he is replaced so the plan and future vision has then changed. I can remember saying this years ago and that is you keep a core of two or three players from which you build and over the course of two seasons you clear out the rest and replace those players. Turning a club of this size around is a big job and everyone who supports this club would need patience with no expectations. This stripping bare the cupboard and replacing with a better standard of player would be a 5 year plan which is a realistic time line. Look at the likes of Liverpool and Arsenal and how attention to detail under the same manager took time to create a foundation before an attack on winning the league was even possible. When you compare Manchester United to other clubs in the top 4 they are shambolic and are lacking the quality players required to run or sustain a bid on winning the title. Manchester United are further away every time they replace their managers as it is a start over process each time. Michael Carrick or Ole Gunnar Solskjaer were never realistic choices of being the clubs manager and was just the club being in a fairy tale mode thinking it was possible. As a business Manchester United has made a financial loss for 7 consecutive years yet somehow this is fine for the owners as they have drained the club up to a tune of £2.3 billion since 2012. The club serves their purpose as a financial cow for their other sporting teams they own and was never about dominating the football scene in England or Europe. Staying in the top 4 however is or was the plan due to the financial benefits of being involved in the European competitions.
[source](https://www.google.com/search?q=premier+league+tables&oq=premier+league+tables&gs_lcrp=EgZjaHJvbWUyBggAEEUYOTINCAEQABiRAhiABBiKBTIKCAIQABiABBi0BzIHCAMQABiABDIHCAQQABiABDIHCAUQABiABDIPCAYQABgUGIcCGIAEGLQHMgoIBxAAGIAEGLQHMgoICBAAGIAEGLQHMgoICRAAGIAEGLQH0gEJNjk2N2owajE1qAIIsAIB&sourceid=chrome&source=chrome.rb&ie=UTF-8) The club currently sits in 14th spot and depending how results go today they could rise or drop to 17th spot which is depressing if you are a Manchester United fan. This was always on the cards with the quality of players at the club. The lower they are in the league the harder it becomes to attract the top players so this could be a much longer than a 5 year plan.
[source](https://www.skysports.com/premier-league-table) A quick update as another loss drops the team down the table one point above relegation so they are deep in the mire and a massive struggle to pull themselves out of this mess.

...and yes, the rain came down the next day, as you will see in the second part of the post.
![061.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/papilloncharity/EoCiXKjmX2ZBP9EdgNjiNbpaTarBsXgpYdLokKHyySVF9jjvELErVPNfSC67nhMqFre.jpg)

Something different in here, as at first I will show you two examples about the contents of this post. First the sun halo (Tag shot), and then the evidence of rain (1 shot).
Then I will share the rest of the sun halo shots, and finally the rest of the wet squirrel shots. 

I have seen many sun halo views, and even posted about them, with a clear explanation of how they are formed, but then we moved to a farm in another province, and I became big friends with the farm laborers. One day, another sun halo appeared, and I was surprised when he shouted out that rain is on its way. What? I asked him how he knew, and then he said that the sun halo was their rain sign.

Ha! I didn't believe him and told him that I think that it's an old wife's tale. Well, it turned out that he was right, as it rained on the next day. The same thing happened now as you will see the evidence in this post. So, look at the first two shots and you will see for yourself that it is true, as the sun halo is indeed a rain sign. In the future when you see a sun halo, then don't plan a picnic the next day. Lol.      

And here's the evidence that a sun halo is a rain sign, as this happened on the next day.
![021.JPG](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/papilloncharity/23wMepumLVVPgRoTVe8RpbrX6fGpMqDjtKcyzFjx6Bf97d9Y8ZmcdAniHQYJfu9nDu58F.JPG)

I tried to take a bird shot in the sky, but then I saw a part of the halo in the right-hand top of the picture. 
![054.JPG](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/papilloncharity/Eou98YJicbnyTj3qcRuhKadzfjbCozg4ATW1rcrMUefQTaQnZpRy5WMktgWPDUb3CL9.JPG)

So, I jumped into the car and travelled around to get some more sun halo shots.
![056.JPG](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/papilloncharity/23wMWbAJM7Z5SFtAGgyQk82mL6mQjsrMomHQqweWzB8xLfuGMS3Tg7vmLSnuwcbtovgHE.JPG)

![058.JPG](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/papilloncharity/EonkUdhHRJHD6kXV8E8hYnXsM9aAjXJ3xHg2LbhwCLkZodTfRXkPvZV7dLbc7ojHe1d.JPG)

**Here below is a short description in Wikipedia about how the halos are formed.**

*The ice crystals responsible for halos are typically suspended in cirrus or cirrostratus clouds in the upper troposphere (5–10 km (3.1–6.2 mi)), but in cold weather they can also float near the ground, in which case they are referred to as diamond dust. The particular shape and orientation of the crystals are responsible for the type of halo observed. Light is reflected and refracted by the ice crystals and may split into colors because of dispersion. The crystals behave like prisms and mirrors, refracting and reflecting light between their faces, sending shafts of light in particular directions.*

[Source](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Halo_(optical_phenomenon))

![063.JPG](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/papilloncharity/EogNHqFveVW27D1azL4g3Ge46qomkCeoDQ8DMtjNFQdUUiXqnboXeGwaCGF2rRzxFsr.JPG)

**Okay, now I will show you the rest of the wet squirrel shots below.** 

Look what appeared on a beam above our study window. You can see that he only glanced down to check if I had seen him. 
![014.JPG](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/papilloncharity/244V2FMaU4UiZPw3yqkxrqdwdDeWr2FEf3LYPPpHXgkFrUSTZNfTjP8D4yLLbiYD3rFHL.JPG)

So, I glanced back and then he gave me a full on stare: *Saying Hey are you blind? Can't you see how wet I am? Now please come and give me some nuts!* 
![016.JPG](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/papilloncharity/2432U4xMQNvWVabhDjHoFbKvwzo8Pah5fUMF2v66zHLvXJfnQyRjKteeHe4NuHeFowiKH.JPG)

![017.JPG](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/papilloncharity/23tveWMCDtexAoTNdaSteyBg6ry2X8ceRpkqPbAvopK3TyjfCm66kr4U8ghvTegWRvbFQ.JPG)

Yep! He won the day, and my wife gave him plenty nuts (raw peanuts). 
![019.JPG](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/papilloncharity/EoGyM8SnWeGDnzo2ba4hbkxchK2ZPFHTFvHR33jQVfiN5tSDMaUF8rqGhu1CbpRBx17.JPG)

Can you believe that the wet little squirrel did not eat all of the nuts, but rather ran to bury most of them? Instead, he ran on to the lawn on the sidewalk (pavement) at the front of our house to bury the nuts in different spots. I just hope that he was not planting a peanut farm. Lol. Yes, I may joke, but we got into trouble once when the squirrels planted nuts in the flowerbeds of some neighbours. They forgot where they planted the nuts and they started to come up as peanut plants. But we moved to another place and thankfully nobody here minds where the squirrels plant their nuts. 
Such is life. 

I hope you enjoyed the pictures and the story.

Photos and words by Zac Smith. No AI and no Photoshop. All-Rights-Reserved.

Camera: Canon PowershotSX70HS Bridge camera. 

Until next time. Shalom!

result.body: [source](https://www.inss.org.il/publication/northern-sea-route/) There is not much information available with regard to the Northern Sea Route even though strategically it is regarded as very hot property as a trading route. The only reason we do not have more news or hear much about this shipping route is largely due to western media down playing the importance. The route is regarded more as a back door or shortcut into Europe as it is only accessible for 5 months of the year due to the pack ice. Once the Russians and Chinese have sufficient ice breaking class vessels it becomes a front door accessible all year round. We know the Chinese when they target a certain area then it is only a matter of time being less than 5 years before this is the new reality. The numbers of shipping transits are telling a different story with 104 confirmed transits by 30th September. Last year only 103 vessels made the trip and what the figures do not tell you is there are currently 45 vessels transiting this route which will bring the total close to 150 for the year which is a 50% growth. Oil and LNG tankers are the biggest growth with over 2.5 million tons being exported to the Far East. there were 4 container transits from East to West with none destined for Russia and were all Europe bound. 2025 only had one such voyage so the growth is taking place even if it is at a slow pace. Sanctions have slowed Russia's export capabilities yet at the same time they are not exactly that affective. The Vostok Oil project which is in the far north of Russia has been delayed for years and is now officially open. The project consists of a nearly 800 kilometer pipeline and a Port on the Taimyr Peninsula. This project may have taken 4 years to complete with all companies involved under heavy Western sanctions yet somehow this never stopped the completion of the project. The reality is sanctions do not work and it is the ice coverage that sets the pace as this week many tankers were waiting for assistance after being trapped in ice. The shadow fleet which is mainly consisting of ageing tankers that would normally have been scrapped are not ice class vessels so the risks for the entire Arctic region having an oil spill or worse are high. The EU would love access to the Northern Sea Route and has called on the US and Canada to increase their military presence in the area through adding security. The EU's Artic Policy is more about maritime surveillance and observing with an emphasis on ice melt along with monitoring the shipping numbers. As the numbers grow which is expected then the route becomes more commercially viable and would require more maritime security. The truth is many are guessing the exact numbers of what Russia is exporting along the route each year and the route is becoming far busier even under sanctions. The 20 million barrels of crude exported by Russia this year represents 1% of the seaborne crude exports so one has to ask where is the balance of 99% being reported? The figures are all Western media figures and are not representative of what is actually happening along the NSR. When you take into account the size of the shadow fleet which is estimated to be more than 1300 tankers strong that is capable of moving nearly 140 million million barrels of crude oil in just one trip. The shadow fleet represents nearly 20% of all tankers globally. Then putting that information into context we have been told the 20 million barrels exported by Russia to China seems a little light. The actual figure is between the official 800 million barrels per year and unofficial 2 billion barrels per year. I would not believe only 20 million barrels were exported along the NSR this year. Russia also exports out of the Port of Primorsk located in the Baltic Sea which accounts for nearly 50% of Russia's crude exports. This is where the latest US diesel exports are originating from. Russia and Indonesia met earlier this month to plan a pilot voyage from Indonesia to Europe in 2027 to calculate the time and costs saved for future exports. A pilot voyage would require Russia's involvement throughout the voyage as it looks to work closer with Russia.

I love my big north facing deck. 

Okay so don't say that with a kiwi accent. 

But seriously, it's pretty special - it's a sun trap, so even if it's cold and windy elsewhere, it's a sun trap, so you can catch warmth like a lizard. 

This morning I took a few snaps before I (sadly) went to work. The morning sun was already warm, and this time of year, it's just *golden* magic. 

I have to say I love the succulents. They're architecturally groovy, and I dont have to water them as much as other plants, though I still do. 

![6722.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/riverflows/23xAeH3Gg66qbnhnSDCmc4r2jX7Ww5DpQPHaE5sxdw6syZNozZBQp5b9KZ9hCzDs6Bhmk.jpg)

And they're easy to get for free, sneaking cuttings from the neighbours or friends or existing cactus. This pretty bluey-grey and pink flowering one came from across the road. There's a fan aloe in there too, and another succulent from a rather fast growing one that seems to pretty much plant itself. 

![6724.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/riverflows/23uFPqTCW6axUbD3pP3ya9ziUSnREvT7ZfBQqCN14kPJuzmqzgHLMGokzG7v9P7vCZep9.jpg)

![6723.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/riverflows/EoCi4RQMksW9BszhBigzJmpYrivXRBbt7xbKa4dsVEnnCJ79No61fQjkgt3T5hJuHN4.jpg)


I've been replacing some of the potted plants with various succulents. This one is catching up because I'd just shoved it in the ground from Mum cutting branches off hers. 

![6728.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/riverflows/EoK6PzPKvQJA5ScE5N2cL2rmUAeS4rYGQZxAYM8xBaSJLokdg6jkke39Xhv3KWFoBEo.jpg)

![6727.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/riverflows/EpLe3YD2QrCZ7chYEJME97cw1hJF9sfe2SA9y3pJhVNkBRud8y7mhJsdQQdcUP2TVU8.jpg)

A lot of the pots I had inside have been replaced now by self watering pots and have migrated outside to be cactus pots. Between them are shells and rocks I've picked up from the beach - a magpie collection of things that make me happy. I love the new 'breakfast' bar or dinner bar or even wine bar that looks over the garden. 

Below this free lounger is given a new life with a couple of screws and wood glue. The leucodendron really doesn't mind the dry. 

![6726.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/riverflows/EoyP39sYg9d1veK3hL2R6ttELDteMM12PSsQS2exxvESUD5FuHJ44VTLfUwKBRBLHbd.jpg)

The deck is big enough for various chairs that chase the shade. If it's windy we can't have the umbrella up. 

![6725.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/riverflows/EopsSPAHE2Ar4MqGy3uDGtiGQ2L2xCLitza2JQUWX195DpgEgNpZwkjZtnJMh8VAyyW.jpg)

Here you can see the view from one end of the breakfast bar. There's a *lot* of native trees that attract kookaburras and parrots and wattle birds. Most directions you can barely see neighbour's roofs. That's our shed roof there - it needs replacing. 


![6721.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/riverflows/23wMQENBwxcSkPTx3kcQysSG9cwye9529S9V8k9k81usgpSzYKdFddWHWyiTvMTsc9kUB.jpg)

And of course, I love the aerial view it affords - a great spot for a cuppa and to think about how everything looks visually and what needs doing, or seeing if I can spot my secateurs or phone from above, haha! 

![6718.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/riverflows/23tvXqsFBXffVf8vTS9Cjj5WCSzXYWSLvcotKaGvR2dNsmHUoZBw8NTqHfr91uwxJqDTm.jpg)

Once that orange calenduala goes to seed, there will be another circle paver there so that it invites people to the bench (i'm hoping to find a better one off marketplace for free) as it's a lovely spot to catch the winter sun. 

![6719.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/riverflows/Eou8GWMWRLThzKQAyYPFa2YKnC7CbYMBt7YJL2bYHwuLbchUS26rnBuc2UJjzA6kZyW.jpg)

This kangaroo paw doesn't mind the pot. I was given it two years ago when Dad died so I'm hoping it'll keep going. In the background that bucket is always full of water to rinse my feet off after a surf before I take sand inside, and it provides water for a watering can I use to water the deck succulents without dragging the hose up the deck. 

![6720.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/riverflows/EorzNNchgUGZFpfpWaqCaFR1vFvHs8qp2dAcDta39EPvhEVvyicXBc8Brnsc13QLyF6.jpg)

Here's another aerial view of the raised beds. I can swear at cabbage moths from any angle, it seems. 

![6717.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/riverflows/EonjyMz6ypdSN7XXECf1vT2rS4TX6GiVbsH1Zaa6vJXjF9Nabi3M213QUtV8C5ZBqcw.jpg)

I got all the way through this and forgot to show you the whole of my big deck! 

![6735.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/gardenhive/23xox9wkCudFA86zVfbHepNxKdwS8qdqxv9nsjyt4bo8Zm82cNWsvsEx7gFThaRRpwVe1.jpg)

That's from the lower garden. It was definitely something the realestate agent was relying on to sell the house, as the rest of it needed work, but I've been pleasantly suprised with actually how much value it adds to my life.

Back again for #BeerSaturday after being away yesterday for a little adventure! Our good friend @detlev is still settling back into the groove so we should start the drinkin and warm the pub up for his return.! This week, I am back from the big city with a trunk full of beer and tales to tell.
![image.png](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/zekepickleman/2466AdGtfg5Nn2foZ5ARrscGywNrmNCoURwPZQLaHdMtLutq4VPapWLx8HBmXmpCZZ22v.png)

The Pint of the week is usually a social beer enjoyed out on the town, one of the best ways to share a pint. Exactly how I enjoyed this one at the end of a long Saturday. In the background, we have a Seven Sons Amber Lagerby [Black Donnelly's Brewing](https://www.black-donnellys.com/our-beer/) as is preferred by our brewmaster. I opted to take one for the team and actually didn't hate this [Lake of Bays Pumpkin Ale](lakeofbaysbrewing.ca/collections/beer/products/pumpkin-ale) I am not a fan of pumpkin in the slightest and usually would taste a new beer over one I already know I like. Those things aside, I STILL haven't found a pumpkin ale I didn't find surprisingly good. The streat continues!

![IMG_0483.jpg](https://images.hive.blog/DQmaZJqi3VCa19ofCieB2bzKXUW1QkZbs36bJQ8WTNemCTW/IMG_0483.jpg)
Whenever life takes me down the road to the big city, I insist upon a visit to perhaps my favourite brewery over the years: [Great Lakes Brewery](www.greatlakesbeer.com) Primarily because of the long list of IPAs they release, and also because there are weekly limited run beers that you can only catch fresh in their tap room. Here is what they had fresh in the fridge to take home.
![IMG_0484.jpg](https://images.hive.blog/DQmfHPKvjcTC1Jv9d1uWw5vT8xuFdwvdinkqR4u6qwdb9Kv/IMG_0484.jpg)
I also love to catch a pint in the tap room as there are even more beers that are only available on tap. Loving those hops shaped lights too.
![image.png](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/zekepickleman/2466AdGtfg5Nn2foZ5ARrscGywNrmNCoURwPZQLaHdMtLutq4VPapWLx8HBmXmpCZZ22v.png)
# Brew SLAM!
![IMG_0492.jpg](https://images.hive.blog/DQmPyR5KHCeUcrSr1SAGmDPi1JnNoRdwv4AbE9DbPdk2GNy/IMG_0492.jpg)
Once per year, we head into [Toronto Brewing Supply](www.torontobrewing.ca) as they are a host of the largest brewing competition in the province, [Brew Slam](www.gtabrews.ca/brew-slam/)
![IMG_0491.jpg](https://images.hive.blog/DQmX1Qc7Z7nrhoG8arhPTFabL1wE27o1DZvdQLmYPPs3Bca/IMG_0491.jpg)
This year, we are entering our award winning Amber Ale as well as a nice bold and hoppy 7.1% New England IPA. Up to 500 entries are made by brewers all around so the competition is stiff. Still, neat to get in there and maybe we will be beer famous on another level! Should know the results by November 21st. ![image.png](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/zekepickleman/2466AdGtfg5Nn2foZ5ARrscGywNrmNCoURwPZQLaHdMtLutq4VPapWLx8HBmXmpCZZ22v.png) # Supply Run!
![IMG_0497.jpg](https://images.hive.blog/DQmcKxicc33mGp7uH5MLo29gAZKL5iwk5D1n3RwutwfSE9W/IMG_0497.jpg)
Now you know what $650 worth of hops looks like! We have stepped up our procudement process with accounts with an industrial sized supplier for our brewing supplies. We go through so much grain and hops with our operation, it pays to buy in larger packages and it is unbelievable how much per ounce/gram price comes down when you do so.
![IMG_0498.jpg](https://images.hive.blog/DQmS361VBDAfUfQQeNsEmAEJHAFEVKQUemBq1EM9fKXuEG4/IMG_0498.jpg)
Now you also know how happy brewmaster is when he received his order! Here he is proudly displaying his 11 pound (5kg) baby which should be enough hops for a year or so. All stocked up with fresh grains, we also are fully set up with Mosaic, Citra, Amarillo and Nelson Sauvin hops in large quantities for all of our IPA needs. Gonna be a delicious year.

工作的时候，偶尔会从楼下听到一声蛤蟆叫：“呱！”

起初我还挺纳闷，园区里虽然有个水池，但里面根本没水，这蛤蟆是从哪里冒出来的呢？

直到今天上午，我站在阳台上，一边喝咖啡，一边发呆。恰好看到一辆🚗从楼下经过，停好车后，车灯闪了一下，紧接着就传来了那个熟悉的声音：

“呱！”

这下总算明白了，闹了半天，原来根本不是蛤蟆在叫，而是汽车发出的声音。囧

现在的汽车锁车提示音，都已经这么有个性了吗？😂

![_8.jpg](https://images.hive.blog/DQmUQyohLSxD582TxEDcxrmDuwx6Xy4oukoeShnrnpoLZfa/_8.jpg)

下午的时候，老婆突然发来一条信息，劈头盖脸地质问我：

“你还管不管你儿子了？”

我一看，顿时有点懵，这又是怎么回事？

紧接着，老婆发来一张截图，原来是老师发给她的消息。

原来，道法老师找孩子妈妈告状来了。老师说，老大这学期开学以来，布置的道法作业就从来没写过。上周老师刚批评过他，本以为这周多少会有所改善，就算做不到彻底改正，起码也该有所收敛吧？

没想到，今天周一开学，老大的道法作业依旧是“外甥打灯笼——照旧（舅）”。这可把老师气坏了，直接找妈妈告状，还要求以后每次的道法作业都必须由家长签字。

哎呀妈呀，我一看，就这点事，晚上回去跟老大说一下不就行了嘛！心里正这么想着，手指一滑，顺手发了个哭笑不得的表情。

没想到，这下可坏事了。老婆以为我是在笑话她，顿时火气更大，接着又把我劈头盖脸地数落了一顿。

好吧，咱好男不跟女斗，暂且不跟她一个女人计较了。囧

至于老大的作业嘛，晚上回去还是得好好跟他谈谈。毕竟，老话说得好：子不教，父之过。老师都已经找上门来了，这事总不能再当没发生过吧！

老大这孩子，自小就淘气，干过很多荒唐事。闯祸更是不计其数，上个星期刚从高处摔下来，差点酿成大祸，吓了我一大跳。今天又来这一出，真是。。。

唉，这孩子，什么时候能让他爹省点心啊。😳😳

![1000236868.png](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/dreamrona/23wqwVZ8DxAnDageUEgEWSchc7YR8iRAn3RgjbpbRfZcEMeSCfcvXEr3khx2GzrEcMNEa.jpg)



Hello, everyone! How are you today?

For me, one of the things that makes me think every day is food. Haha! Sometimes, I am still eating my breakfast, but my mind is already asking, “What will I cook for our next meal?” As a mother, I always think about what to prepare for my family. We need to eat every day, and buying ingredients can be expensive.



![1000236715.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/dreamrona/23x1FTybSXjuVpczWAFWsbFNTdsvD6QiK86ZozK3MehsztK2pX9aZWjkYtDiCqxmg8xgC.jpg)

![1000236716.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/dreamrona/23vsG6MtFKvNPgfQFr2MctBbe4RvhQ8m94mgSFS3oexTr28Uh48DmzH6uxi7R3fehYV36.jpg)

But today, I am happy because I did not spend money on our main dish. Guess what? I just went to my mother's garden!

My mother has gabi or taro plants in her garden, so I picked some taro roots and stems to cook for our lunch. Here in the mountain, we need to be resourceful. If we have vegetables around us, why not use them to prepare food for our family? We do not need to buy everything, especially when we can harvest something from the garden.



![1000236717.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/dreamrona/23tveWMVAkxgqcAykuYoP14ZeYrFRYmfMGjr19Gn7kgagkYpY6ps6pBd429cXDi5J788L.jpg)

After picking the gabi, I cleaned the leaves and stems and sliced them into pieces. Haha! Do not expect my slices to have the same size because I did not measure them. For me, what is important is that I clean them properly before cooking.



![1000236721.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/dreamrona/23wqik3JAT9tqMix3ozWffjgV1WRorznCh1X6hyaJTcUwdEWWgy9BoDJaW2UPtm6zTiUJ.jpg)

I also grated a coconut to get fresh coconut milk. We have to do some work before we can enjoy our food, but that is okay. This is part of our simple life here in the countryside. After preparing everything, I was ready to cook our laing or ginataang gabi.

![1000236185.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/dreamrona/23w2oGnkauRhqLczca9iDBwKJRwssJqgLbNnBgo7gZrnLJgqPaKDaDrLrmqh4sYdV7nz9.jpg)

While I was cooking, my neighbor and friend suddenly arrived. She brought me a pasalubong from Iloilo, and I was surprised because she gave me a lot of dried fish! I felt so happy because even though she went somewhere far, she still remembered me.



I also gave her some vegetables from our garden as my way of saying thank you. I believe that sharing does not always have to involve money. Sometimes, the vegetables we grow ourselves are already enough to make someone happy.

By the way, have you heard people say that when a selfish person cooks taro, it becomes itchy? Haha! I do not know if that is true, but maybe I am not selfish because our laing did not become itchy! Just kidding!



![1000236787.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/dreamrona/23u5y7W8gYLDTGJvx2zQLrBxg2GNstVcajDxAu5VuUdUSLU9pZE246qF5HQU33TVKnmyr.jpg)

Finally, our lunch was ready. I served our laing with fried dried fish, and we enjoyed eating together. What a simple but satisfying meal!

I am happy because I did not spend money on our main dish today. Thanks to my mother's garden and my thoughtful friend, we had a delicious lunch.



![1000236792.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/dreamrona/23wgPhongSnrYKXrmoLearSgDzd2TswTvEjdB8Ba5nBXNzwK6NPq8CFeGg7Zd4feegFpE.jpg)

Living in the mountain teaches me to appreciate simple things. If we have a garden, we should take care of it because it can help feed our family. For me, having food to serve on the table without spending much money is already a blessing.


![1000236791.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/dreamrona/23wMcbgrkMBNhsHdu81XWYoP6RZrVqxY5jgd29KCjui6wkW9FAY57VeHGDAeDKhABEJCG.jpg)

Thank you for reading my story. This is my own picture and the lead photo was edited in chatgtp to inhance the image. 

Have a nice day. 💛

I was reading in The Week a summary of Mihir Sharma’s Bloomberg column about Jensen Huang’s verdict on Britain. Apparently we have plenty of talent but not enough entrepreneurial spirit. Give us a million ways to succeed and we’ll find the one reason not to bother.

There’s probably something in that. But whenever a billionaire tells everyone else to take more risks, I do wonder whether we’re talking about quite the same thing.

Losing money when you already have more than you could ever spend is rather different from losing the money you need for next month’s rent.

### We’re quite happy to gamble on houses

The strongest part of Sharma’s argument, IMO, is about property. Too much British wealth is tied up in housing, which is treated as the sensible option, while backing something new is regarded as a bit reckless.

The ONS estimated that net property wealth accounted for 40% of household wealth in Great Britain in 2020–22. These are historical figures, with survey limitations, but they give some idea of how central housing is to our finances.

Obviously, owning somewhere to live isn’t the same as speculating. People need homes. But there’s a difference between providing housing and organising your whole idea of financial success around its price going up.

If buying a property looks like the safest route to getting ahead, why be surprised when people choose that over developing a product, employing people and spending years wondering whether the business will survive?

Calling this a national character flaw lets the incentives off rather lightly.

### Ambition doesn’t pay the bills

And Britain clearly does have people willing to build businesses. The British Business Bank’s July 2026 equity update reported £12.3 billion invested in smaller businesses during 2025, although that was down 4%. AI firms took a record 44% of the total.

That hardly suggests a country where everyone has given up and gone home. It does raise a question about which businesses investors are prepared to support. Having a good idea outside the fashionable sector might be rather less exciting to the people writing the cheques.

Then there’s the individual starting position. Imagine two people with the same idea. One has family money and somewhere to live rent-free. The other has childcare costs, rent and no savings. Both are supposedly free to become entrepreneurs, but only one can comfortably survive a year of making nothing.

The second person taking a salaried job hasn’t necessarily demonstrated a lack of imagination. They might just have done the sums.

![image.png](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/revisesociology/23vhwMV4cuFtTpFAUdVLTUbDhH1aPP6CsNz9F1v8ZsYPxzNRTQjFcnwxFrc9D69smgu36.jpg)


This is why I find the sneering at protection against risk a bit odd. Some security could make trying something new more realistic. Affordable housing, reliable childcare and support when things go wrong would give more people room to experiment.

### Final thoughts

Huang may be right that Britain needs to think bigger. Sharma is certainly right to question our attachment to property.

But “be more entrepreneurial” is fairly cheap advice unless we also ask who has the money, time and security to act on it.

I’d be more impressed by a programme that made failure survivable for ordinary people than another lecture about national ambition. We might discover there’s plenty of entrepreneurial spirit once having a go doesn’t mean putting your family’s stability on the line.

Este fin de semana estuvo cargado de entrenamiento, aprendizaje y algunas lecciones que me llevo para seguir mejorando como corredora.

Viernes: volvimos a la técnica de carrera.

Después de un tiempo sin hacer esta clase, ¡por fin regresamos! Para mí, es una de las sesiones más importantes, porque no se trata solo de correr, sino de aprender a hacerlo mejor: mejorar mi postura, ganar potencia, prevenir lesiones y lograr una mejor economía de carrera.

Nuestro instructor, José Rodríguez, el maracucho, tiene una metodología de enseñanza que me gusta mucho. Sabe transmitir sus conocimientos, demuestra lo que enseña y tiene muy buen manejo del grupo. Aunque hubo una situación incómoda con una persona durante la clase, eso no impidió que aprovecháramos una sesión que, en general, estuvo muy buena. 

Sábado: toco  zona 2 
Ando con malestar de gripe, pero igual toco cumplir. La idea era salir más temprano, pero terminé comenzando a las 8:00 a. m. y, a esa hora, el sol ya estaba implacable.

No pude mantener los ritmos que venía haciendo, alrededor de 6:00 min/km, y terminé con un promedio de 6:30-6:27 min/km. Sin embargo, lo importante no era correr más rápido, sino respetar el objetivo del entrenamiento. Conseguí mantener un buen porcentaje en zona 2, trabajando esa base aeróbica que me permite desarrollar mayor resistencia y sostener mejor los esfuerzos.

Todo esto forma parte de la preparación con la mirada puesta en el CAF. Cada entrenamiento cuenta, incluso esos días en los que el cuerpo no está al 100 %.

Domingo: 11 kilómetros y buenas sensaciones. 

La indicación de mi entrenador, mi Capi, fue clara: comenzar el primer kilómetro con calma e ir aumentando el ritmo progresivamente, guiándome por mis sensaciones. Y así lo hice.

Aprovechamos que había una caminata y una carrera por la avenida Francisco de Miranda, con la vía cerrada, para hacer nuestra sesión. ¡Y qué casualidad! Era prácticamente la misma ruta de la carrera de Bancaribe, cuyo reconocimiento estaba previsto, pero que finalmente no se realizó por parte de la organización. Así que el equipo aprovechó la oportunidad y terminó haciendo su propio reconocimiento.

El sol también estuvo candela, pero las sensaciones durante el recorrido fueron buenas. Como le dije a mi Capi, no di el 100 %, pero me sentí bien en muchos tramos. Y eso también es importante: aprender a escuchar el cuerpo y entender que no todos los días son para exigirse al máximo.

Ahora bien, hay algo que tengo que corregir: ¡necesito meterle más combustible a mi cuerpo! ⛽️

Tengo que aumentar el consumo de carbohidratos y cuidar especialmente lo que como antes de correr. Puede ser una buena fuente de carbohidratos o un gel, según el entrenamiento, pero no puedo pretender rendir si no le doy al cuerpo la energía que necesita.

Después de los kilómetros, terminamos comiendo en un sitio de comida maracucha aquí mismo en Chacao. ¡Comí sabroso! Aunque creo que me excedí un poquito, porque entre la comida y el malestar de gripe, mi estómago decidió quejarse. 😂 Digamos que no fue el mejor cierre gastronómico, pero sí uno bastante disfrutable.

Y así termina mi fin de semana deportivo: técnica, zona 2, 11 kilómetros progresivos, aprendizaje y algunos ajustes que debo hacer para seguir avanzando.

Me quedo con las buenas sensaciones, con el trabajo acumulado y con la certeza de que entrenar también significa aprender a escuchar el cuerpo, alimentarlo bien y entender que el progreso no depende de dar el 100 % todos los días, sino de ser constante y entrenar con inteligencia.

Seguimos sumando, seguimos aprendiendo y seguimos corriendo. 
Próxima parada: ¡Nike Run!

I grew up hearing the name Vittorio De Sica. He was a giant in Italian cinema, but I dismissed him as just another popular filmmaker.  That was until last week, when I watched his 1970 movie, *Sunflower*.  The movie is annoying in places, and at times seems like an implausible romantic melodrama.  Also, it comes across as a showcase for Sophia Loren, who at the time was married to its producer, Carlo Ponti.  Despite its shortcomings, *Sunflower* left an impression on me, so much so that I looked up other De Sica films. Then I discovered what a truly great filmmaker this director/producer was.

Vittorio De Sica's greatest films were made right after WWII, which ended in 1945.  The films were raw, difficult to watch because of their emotional impact. *Sunflower* is not that. Made twenty-five years after the war ended, this movie is essentially a love story with war as a backdrop. 

In his early post-WWII films, De Sica laid the foundation for a movement known as Italian neorealism.  Neorealism was a response by De Sica and other filmmakers to post-World War II Italy. The filmmakers were working in a country that had been physically devastated by the war.

*Naples, 1944, [public domain](https://commons.wikimedia.org/wiki/File:Santa_Chiara_(Naples),_3.jpg) photo by Maria Napoli*
![](https://images.hive.blog/DQmRtt3ENSBs3qEZ6tu7HJhEswnedP8yCgfgcd4ToUrjkNv/Santa_Chiara_(Naples),_3.jpg)


 No institutional film industry existed, so movies were made with the material at hand.  Cameras in streets.  Impoverished people, non-actors, populated the scene. The result was ground-breaking and brilliant.  

By the time *Sunflower* was made, in 1970, the film industry had returned to Italy. This movie has a polished look.  Even though the first scene takes place right after the war ended, the streets are clean.  People are well fed, well dressed.

The female lead, Giovanna, played by Sophia Loren, is in distress but she is not hungry, not struggling to pay her rent or find employment. She is upset because her husband, Antonio, played by Marcello Mastroianni, has not returned from the war, and yet she has not been told if he is alive or dead.  

The government cannot tell Giovanna the status of her husband, so she decides to go find him on her own.  This quest takes her to the Soviet Union, where he had been sent to fight. 

The movie is an obvious showcase for Sophia Loren, and the camera does linger on her face and body longer than it might have if another actor had been in that role. She  acquits herself well enough in most scenes, but I have seen roles in which she was more effective.

The best scenes in the movie are shot in the Soviet Union.  The movie was a rare collaboration at the time between Western filmmakers and the Soviet Union.  It is in the Soviet scenes that De Sica reverts to his neorealist technique.  While I found these more artistically successful than the rest of the movie, Sophia Loren was not a good fit as she traipsed around a vast graveyard where fallen soldiers were buried.  

Giovanna does find her husband in the Soviet Union.  He has married a Russian woman and has had a child with her.  He has started a new life.

*Giovanna Discovers Her Husband Has Found a New Love*
https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=XvoxMD8Y2iE

This development is consistent with De Sica's earlier war-themed movies.  War disrupts. War destroys.  Here, though, there is a less brutal expression of war's cruelty than in the early classics.

Do Giovanna and Antonio end up together?  What happens to the Russian wife and child?  These are questions that will not be answered in this blog. You'll have to watch the movie to find out.  Should you watch it?  I think so, but don't expect too much.  Don't expect too much from the script, or the actors.

The film is entertaining and a worthy watch, mostly, I believe, because it is an introduction to De Sica--if his work is unfamiliar to you.  After watching this, it would be a good idea to  move on to *Bicycle Thieves*. This masterpiece is considered to be one of the greatest movies ever made.  Also, view *Umberto D*. This film ranks, again, among the best and most influential movies in cinema history.

**WWII and Italian Cinema**

*Clip of Benito Mussolini in Milan, 1934*
https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=Wnl2IPQujmY
Vittorio De Sica once said, "We are all guilty". To understand what he meant by that, and to place the statement in the context of his war-themed films, we have to know something about Italy's role in WWII.  

Italian leader Benito Mussolini, in 1925, declared that democratic liberalism was dead in Italy and the country was a fascist state. After that Italy was in thrall to this man some historians regard as a [narcissistic sociopath](https://www.researchgate.net/publication/371563601_Mussolini_-From_delinquency_to_psychopathy_with_narcissistic_personality_disorder_First_Draft). Many Italians, perhaps, did not see Mussolini for what he was.  Vittorio De Sica stated in a New York Times article:
>  I personally did not take Mussolini seriously in the beginning. He was too much like a clown. It was only after he declared war that I took him seriously, and then it was too late.

It might be said that, in a way, [the Italian people enabled Mussolini,](https://academic.oup.com/book/49399/chapter-abstract/416649447?redirectedFrom=fulltext) as did De Sica. The leader was very popular, particularly with the industrialists and the ruling class. When Italy finally allied with Germany and entered the war on Germany's side, it was the Italian people who paid the price.  

They rethought their decision midway through the war, staged a coup and arrested Mussolini. However, the Germans rescued him and established  a puppet state in northern Italy. As the Germans withdrew from Italy they were determined to leave nothing behind. They bombed everything in sight.  Not only did the Italians suffer bombing campaigns from the Allies before German withdrawal, but they also suffered devastating losses as German forces left.


The Italian economy was shattered at the end of the war. The clip below gives a hint of what life was like for a common worker at that time:
https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=Vbjcv3Ceilw

In *Sunflower* you see no hint of Italy's wartime destruction.  It looks like everybody that wants a job, has a job.  The toll from war is reckoned by the missing and the dead. 

Are there outstanding performances in this movie? Yes, I think so. Some minor actors acquit themselves more effectively than the marquis stars.  Glauco Onorato, for example, who is known simply as the Returning Soldier, is memorable in his role as he leaves Antonio behind in the snow.  

***Trivia:
[Official persecution](https://encyclopedia.ushmm.org/content/en/article/italy) of Jews began in 1938 under Mussolini--two years before war was declared. Forced deportations followed, starting in 1940. 

It is estimated that [115,000](https://nationalinterest.org/blog/buzz/revealed-the-tragic-story-the-italian-army-froze-death-18497) Italian soldiers died fighting in the Soviet Union during the war.

Vittorio De Sica was not a Fascist.  Before and during the war he was a movie star.  As a matter of fact he starred in more movies than he ever directed.

I hope in future weeks to review some of De Sica's better films. 

I watched this on Kino Lorber, which is a subscription I hold on Amazon Prime Video.


Thank you for reading my blog.  Peace, and health to all.

_Rating: **75/100**_

I've been working this week on finishing the Butter Cloud. The idea behind it all is that we could go back to implementing S3 technology in 3Speak without adding costs to our infrastructure.

![image.png](https://images.hive.blog/DQmVyKYEpiNYnhU1qHg8DU4BCZCaNBPXAGMinie9bmTuNfL/image.png)

I had begun working on Butter Cloud many months ago, and I had an MVP. But of course, one thing is to upload an image or two, and another one entirely is to serve videos.

With that said, the biggest challenge here is to incorporate S3 into our infrastructure without completely abandoning IPFS.

The ingest flow is done through IPFS, and it seems more than obvious that if we are to incorporate Speak Network in the future, IPFS is the only viable answer. But it's almost like dancing on top of rocks without shoes.

At every turn, with every decision, I have to keep in mind that whatever we build has to remain open enough to work with IPFS somewhere in the mix.

How do we inject, if you will, decentralization into centralization? A weird question, I admit, but a valid one right now.

The more I think about it, the more I think I need to build a new service. Something I'm thinking of calling **Video Pulse**. A service responsible for detecting organic plays on videos, both new and old, and keeping those videos on the Hotnode as long as they continue to get played, until they eventually go dormant.

I thought for a minute about incorporating this somewhere into our current stack, but it seems specialized enough to live on its own.

Another challenge that needs solving, and this is because we're literally running 3Speak on a shoestring budget, is how we can add redundancy to our S3 bucket.

IPFS, by its very nature, offers redundancy. Gateways can cache content, and that's before any CDN even gets involved. But S3? That's a different story.

This means that before going live, I'll need to decide how to double up our new MongoDB deployment. It needs a replica for safety. I'll also need to figure out how to double up the Butter Cloud Node server itself, because we can't trust a single VPS to never fail.

Seems like every step I take, I end up writing ten more issues for myself. Ten more questions that need answers.

Like a good friend once said to me:

**These projects grow tentacles.**

MenO
